<!-- pr-reviewer: 71a7fee47351ae5e513b4cfbebfbd04868a7ad28 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge** (a `feat`: at the next cut). No blockers found; three non-blocking notes below.

Reviewed by the M5 reviewer on rules from `upstream/main` (PROCESS_VERSION 76). Safety floor: toolpath, so the checks below were done by running and mutating the code, not by reading only.

## What looks good
- Purely additive: new `adaptive/rest/` module and `raster/conservative.rs` in `camcraft-motion`, plus `mod rest;` and a `pub use`. `rest2d::rest_strategy` and the Pocket operation are untouched, so Adaptive for rest is still refused there until #2033. No `Cargo.toml`, `build.rs`, `.github`, scripts, process files, CHANGELOG or snapshot PNGs touched; no new `camcraft-*` dependency; tests sit in the lowest crate (motion).
- Independence of the test reading: `tests/rest_adaptive/sim.rs` cuts the 12 mm Waterline path into a `stock_sim` column stock and reads plunges/rapids against that simulated stock. The planner works only on its own `Region`/`Raster` built from `RestStock` and never touches `stock_sim`. Plunge and rapid checks run before `measure` cuts the rest path into the simulation, so only the earlier operation's cuts are credited. The proved stock is also asserted not to read smaller than the simulation (`roughed`, `outside == 0`). Shared between planner and test: the load formulas (`load_at_rim`, `rim_for`) and the generator that makes the roughing path. That is fine for a yardstick, but it means the yardstick itself is not independently checked (see note 1).
- No `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` in the new non-test code; float-to-index casts saturate and the raster loops are bounded (`conservative.rs:keep`). Every refusal is by name and, where it has a place, carries the point (`pass.rs` `refusal`: load, entry, crossing; `stock.rs`: no floor, depth below the proved floor, non-finite floor; `mod.rs`: nothing to cut, tool wider than the pocket). The two #2108 refusals (corner too sharp, neck too narrow) are pinned by `a_pocket_corner_too_sharp_to_turn_in_within_the_load_is_refused_by_name` and `a_neck_too_narrow_to_hold_the_load_is_refused_by_name`.
- Provenance lines on every new module; literature cited; decision file `docs/decisions/2031-rest-adaptive.md` present; Changelog and effort lines in the body; conventional subjects.
- The last commit (`71a7fee47`) is confirmed docs-only (`docs/decisions/2031-rest-adaptive.md`, 10+/9-), so the green gate on `9916b459d` covers the code.

## Results (locally, on a trial merge with `upstream/main`; nothing was dispatched to GitHub Actions)
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --test rest_adaptive` | 9 passed, 0 failed (34 s) |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --lib rest` (3 guard-mutation tests, conservative raster, wall vertices, phase radii; plus the existing `adaptive_troch` rest tests) | 11 passed |
| `--test rest2d` / `adaptive_hsm` / `optimal_load` / `machining2d` (neighbours) | 10 / 1 (+5 ignored) / 4 / 66 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

The app and ui suites were not re-run: the diff is motion-only and additive, and the author's gate on the code commit ran them (app 47 binaries ok).

Mutations I ran against the head (each reverted):
1. Conservative growth set to 0 (`conservative_growth() -> 0.0`): `an_island_and_disconnected_rest_areas_are_each_entered_from_proved_space` goes red. Good.
2. The three built-in guard switches (stock / depth / entry): each is asserted red by its own unit test, and all three pass (the pin fails when the guard is off).
3. Entry raster proof removed (`&& self.stock.air(p, p, self.footprint)` deleted) and raster footprint set to 0: all 9 stay green. The polygon proof (`blocked`, material grown by tool radius + half margin) carries every fixture on its own, so the raster half of the double entry proof is not pinned by any test. Not a defect (it is defence in depth), see note 2.

## Requested before merge
None.

## Notes (not blocking)
1. **Load bound and the grid.** The tests hold the measured load to optimal x 1.05 (15.3% of D) on the planner's own D/120 grid, the same grid the planner walks. I re-ran the suite on other measuring grids: at D/80 (the default) `a_conventional_cut_leaving_stock_on_the_walls_keeps_every_law` fails with "the measured load 16.7% of D is past the optimal 14.6%" (the author reports up to 17.4% in a concave corner), so the bound is only as good as the yardstick's grid. D/240 cannot be tried on the larger fixtures (the stock grid is capped at 4096 cells per axis), but the corner fixtures that fit it still passed there, which supports the author's reading that this is the measuring rim over-reading wall on a coarse grid, not real over-engagement. I judge the tests lenient in one respect: nothing pins a ceiling at the default grid. Suggestion for a follow-up, not this PR: add one corner-fixture assertion at D/240 (true load within the bound) and one at D/80 with a stated, documented ceiling (about 1.2 x optimal), so a future change that makes the real load worse cannot hide behind the grid choice. When #2033 wires the operation, whatever default-grid `quality::measure` check the op runs will read these paths above 15.3%, so that follow-up is worth filing before wiring.
2. **Entry raster proof is unpinned** (mutation 3 above). Consider one fixture where the raster refuses a spot the polygon proof allows (a sliver thinner than a cell near a wall), so the "asked of the polygon and of the raster" claim is under test and not only in the doc comment.
3. **`adaptive/raster.rs` is 404 lines** (was 403; +1 for `mod conservative;`). Per the ~400 law this is a note, not a blocker: the growth is one line and the real new code went to a separate file under 100 lines. The next addition there should split the file. All new `rest/` files are under 340 lines.

**Fixes vs Refs #2031:** `Fixes #2031` is right. The issue says "Keep the existing refusal until the required stock and entry proofs are available" and its Done means is "Adaptive runs on proved remaining stock, passes these tests, and refuses unsupported stock or entry cases by name". The generator, the named refusals and every listed test (corner residues, islands, disconnected areas, narrow neck, roughing stopping above the rest floor, each guard mutated separately) are in this PR; the operation wiring is explicitly #2033's (still open, and the PR body states it). Wording suggestion for the PR body only: say that the Pocket refusal stays by design until #2033.

Follow-ups #2108 (sharp corners/necks) and #2109 (air feed about 4x cut length) are named in the PR and the decision file; no action here.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
